title: Existence of a finite-type extension of an ideal
statement:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $W\subseteq X$ be a
quasi-compact open, and let
$\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ be a finite type quasi-coherent ideal.
There exists a finite type quasi-coherent ideal
$\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with
$\mathcal I|_W=\mathcal J$.
More generally, if $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F|_W$ is a finite type
quasi-coherent submodule of the restriction of a quasi-coherent module
$\mathcal F$ on $X$, then $\mathcal G$ is the restriction of a finite type
quasi-coherent submodule of $\mathcal F$.

proof.text:
We prove the more general assertion. First take the inverse image
$\mathcal H$ of $j_*\mathcal G$ under
$\mathcal F\to j_*j^*\mathcal F$, where $j\colon W\hookrightarrow X$.
Since $j$ is quasi-compact and $X$ is quasi-separated, $j_*\mathcal G$ is
quasi-coherent; kernels of maps of quasi-coherent modules are
quasi-coherent. Thus $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and
$\mathcal H|_W=\mathcal G$.

Choose affine opens $V_1,\ldots,V_n$ with
$X=W\cup V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_n$. Inductively suppose that a finite type
submodule $\mathcal G_r\subseteq\mathcal H$ has been constructed on
$W_r=W\cup V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_r$ and restricts to $\mathcal G$ on $W$.
Put $V_{r+1}=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. On $V_{r+1}$ take the inverse image
$\mathcal K$ of the direct image of
$\mathcal G_r|_{W_r\cap V_{r+1}}$ under the restriction map from
$\mathcal H|_{V_{r+1}}$. The same quasi-compact-open direct-image argument
shows that $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent, and by construction its
restriction to $W_r\cap V_{r+1}$ is $\mathcal G_r$. Write
$\mathcal K=\widetilde N$. The intersection is quasi-compact. Cover it by
finitely many basic opens $D(f_i)$ on which $\mathcal G_r$ is generated by
finitely many sections. Because $\mathcal G_r\subseteq\widetilde N$ there,
after shrinking the basic opens if necessary and clearing denominators, those
generators are represented by finitely many elements $x_{ij}\in N$. Let
$N'\subseteq N$ be generated by all $x_{ij}$. Enlarging the denominator
powers when clearing them ensures
$\widetilde{N'}|_{D(f_i)}=\mathcal G_r|_{D(f_i)}$: one inclusion holds by
construction, and the other is checked on the chosen finite generators.
Hence $\widetilde{N'}$ and $\mathcal G_r$ agree on the whole intersection and
glue to a finite type submodule on $W_{r+1}$. Finite induction gives the
required submodule on $X$. Taking $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and
$\mathcal G=\mathcal J$ gives the asserted ideal; compatibility with the
inclusions into $\mathcal O_X$ makes the glued submodule an ideal.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and let $W\subseteq X$ be a
quasi-compact open.

1. If $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ is a finite type quasi-coherent
   ideal, there exists a finite type quasi-coherent ideal
   $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with $\mathcal I|_W=\mathcal J$.
2. If $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent ideal whose
   restriction $\mathcal H|_W$ is of finite type, there exists a finite type
   quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal H$ with
   $\mathcal I|_W=\mathcal H|_W$.

More generally, both assertions hold for quasi-coherent submodules of a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ in place of ideals of
$\mathcal O_X$: a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal F$
with $\mathcal H|_W$ of finite type contains a finite type quasi-coherent
submodule with the same restriction to $W$, and every finite type
quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F|_W$ is the
restriction of a finite type quasi-coherent submodule of $\mathcal F$.

proof.text:
We prove the module versions; the ideal versions are the case
$\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, where all submodules are ideals. Let
$j\colon W\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion; it is quasi-compact because
$W$ is quasi-compact and $X$ is quasi-separated, so direct images along
$j$ (and along the inclusions of the quasi-compact opens below) of
quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent.

*Second assertion.* Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal F$ be quasi-coherent
with $\mathcal G:=\mathcal H|_W$ of finite type. Choose affine opens
$V_1,\ldots,V_n$ with $X=W\cup V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_n$. Inductively suppose
that a finite type quasi-coherent submodule
$\mathcal G_r\subseteq\mathcal H|_{W_r}$ has been constructed on
$W_r=W\cup V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_r$ which restricts to $\mathcal G$ on $W$
(start with $\mathcal G_0=\mathcal G$ on $W_0=W$). Put
$V_{r+1}=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. On $V_{r+1}$ take the inverse image
$\mathcal K$ of the direct image of
$\mathcal G_r|_{W_r\cap V_{r+1}}$ under the restriction map from
$\mathcal H|_{V_{r+1}}$. The same quasi-compact-open direct-image argument
shows that $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent, and by construction
$\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal H|_{V_{r+1}}$ and its restriction to
$W_r\cap V_{r+1}$ is $\mathcal G_r$. Write
$\mathcal K=\widetilde N$. The intersection is quasi-compact. Cover it by
finitely many basic opens $D(f_i)$ on which $\mathcal G_r$ is generated by
finitely many sections. Because $\mathcal G_r\subseteq\widetilde N$ there,
after shrinking the basic opens if necessary and clearing denominators, those
generators are represented by finitely many elements $x_{ij}\in N$. Let
$N'\subseteq N$ be generated by all $x_{ij}$. Enlarging the denominator
powers when clearing them ensures
$\widetilde{N'}|_{D(f_i)}=\mathcal G_r|_{D(f_i)}$: one inclusion holds by
construction, and the other is checked on the chosen finite generators.
Hence $\widetilde{N'}\subseteq\mathcal H|_{V_{r+1}}$ and $\mathcal G_r$
agree on the whole intersection and glue to a finite type submodule
$\mathcal G_{r+1}\subseteq\mathcal H|_{W_{r+1}}$ restricting to
$\mathcal G$ on $W$. Finite induction gives a finite type quasi-coherent
submodule $\mathcal G_n\subseteq\mathcal H$ on $X$ with
$\mathcal G_n|_W=\mathcal H|_W$.

*First assertion.* Given a finite type quasi-coherent
$\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F|_W$, let $\mathcal H$ be the inverse image of
$j_*\mathcal G$ under $\mathcal F\to j_*j^*\mathcal F$. It is
quasi-coherent, being a kernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules, and
$\mathcal H|_W=\mathcal G$ is of finite type. The second assertion gives a
finite type quasi-coherent submodule of $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal F$
restricting to $\mathcal G$ on $W$.
